blocks.text: 54. For this cause then is He Saviour. Now Emmanuel is, being interpreted, With you God; [^irenaeus-demonstration-iv-138] or as a yearning cry [^irenaeus-demonstration-iv-139] uttered by the prophet, such as this: With us shall be God; according to which it is the explanation and manifestation of the good tidings proclaimed. For Behold, He saith, the virgin shall conceive and shall bring forth a son; and He, being God, is to be with us. And, as if altogether astonished [^irenaeus-demonstration-iv-140] at these things, he proclaims in regard to these future events that With us shall be God. And yet again concerning His birth the same. prophet says in another place: Before she that travailed gave birth, and before the pains of travail came on, she escaped and was delivered of a man-child. Thus he showed that His birth from the virgin was unforeseen and unexpected. [^irenaeus-demonstration-iv-141] And again the same prophet says: Unto us a son is born, and unto us a child is given: [^irenaeus-demonstration-iv-142] and his name shall be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God. [^irenaeus-demonstration-iv-143]

irenaeus-demonstration-iv-138.text: The translator has read μεθ᾽ ὑμῶν for μεθ᾽ ἔμῶν : there is no distinction in sound in the later Greek pronunciation.

irenaeus-demonstration-iv-140.text: Cf. c. 71; and Just. M. Ap. 1, 47: θαυμαζόντων τὰ γεγενημένα : Dial. 118: τοῦτο θαυμάζων Ἠσαιὰς ἔφη.

irenaeus-demonstration-iv-141.text: III, xxvi. 2: “ In eo autem quod dixerit: Ipse Dominus dabit signum , id quod erat inopinatum generationis ejus significavit. . . . Sed quoniam inopinata salus hominibus inciperet fieri, Deo adjuvante, inopinatus et partus virginis fiebat, ” etc.

irenaeus-demonstration-iv-142.text: The transposition of “son” and “child” would seem to be an oversight: see however Just. M. Ap. 1, 35 ( παιδίον . . . νεανίσκος ]: and note that the whole passage is quoted differently in c. 56 below.

irenaeus-demonstration-iv-143.text: So in IV, lv. 2: cf. III, xx. 2. So above, c. 40. But in c. 56 we have “Angel of great counsel,” as in III, xvii. 3: cf. Just. M. Dial. 76.
